name: Luke
title: The Beloved Physician
summary: Luke was a physician and Paul's faithful companion. He is the author of the Gospel of Luke and the Acts of the Apostles—together nearly one-quarter of the New Testament. As the only non-Jewish biblical writer, he wrote thoroughly and with historical accuracy about Jesus' life and the early years of the church.

keyEvents.title: Travel Companion with Paul
keyEvents.description: Luke joined Paul in Troas and accompanied him on parts of his missionary journeys. The 'we' passages in Acts show his presence.

keyEvents.title: The Beloved Physician
keyEvents.description: Paul referred to Luke as 'the beloved physician' and his faithful companion.

keyEvents.title: Faithful to the End
keyEvents.description: When Paul was imprisoned in Rome for the last time, Luke was the only one who stayed with him.

keyEvents.title: Author of the Gospel
keyEvents.description: Luke wrote a detailed gospel for Theophilus, based on eyewitness accounts and careful investigation.

keyEvents.title: Historian of the Church
keyEvents.description: Luke continued his account in the Acts of the Apostles, which describes the church's growth from Jerusalem to Rome.
